# Heat and Cool Series

As of 20 July 2025, we have a complete simulation with 85
initializations, each starting with particles in their minimum potential
energy positions, with kinetic energy defined but randomly distributed.
The next series will create heating and cooling from the end of runs in
equilibrium.

I am clearing the environment on 21 July 2025, but I have saved it just
in case via the statement:
`save.image("/media/phil/Original/Users/phils/Documents/DSP/MD/MD2/250721.RData")`

We would like to create eight new series: four heating through the
transition (and through the `Solid1/Solid2` transition), and four
cooling through it. Looking through the data, it appear the following
runs are of interest.

```{r}
#| label: newruns
newruns <- c("S3.0008", "S3.0009","S3.0010","S3.0011", "S3.0043",
             "S3.0044","S3.0045","S3.0046")
knitr::kable( S3DTdiff2[ run %in% newruns, 
                        .(run, Temp=ke.mean.rs, valid, total.steps)])
```

We also need to define a method to track the heat/cool series. We would
like to track the origin of each heat/cool run. Note that the program
always writes the scalar file with the same name as the state file from
which it starts, but adds "heat" to the name (regardless of the value of
`Beta`). The state will be saved original "energy" number will be kept,
with `hnn` appended to it. So the first heated execution from
`S3.0008.0007` will result in the scalar file `S3.0008.0007.heat.csv`,
and the state file `S3h.0008h01.0001.jld2`. Once `S3h.0008h01` reaches
equilibrium (or 4M steps), it can be the source for the next heating or
cooling execution. For example, if it takes five executions to reach
equilibrium, the last execution's scalars will be in
`S3h.0008h01.0005.scalars.csv`, and the state will be saved in
`S3h.0008h01.0006.jld2`. The next heating execution will be
`S3h.0008h02.0000`. Care will be needed to perform diffusion calculation
before heating/cooling, as we are not overtly recording the starting
file, although it will show up in the `.txt` log file.

I created `heatcool()` in `RunScripts.jl` to regularize running
heating/cooling cycles. We want to heat the cold runs until they reach
$T = 0.0208$ and cool the hot runs until they reach $T = 0.004$The first
successful run is below.

It is time consuming to generate each set executions by manually fixing
the start numbers. the following *Julia* regex can be used to
filterm\[1\] filenames into useable groups.

```{r}
#| label: fnames
jld <- paste( "^[A-Za-z0-9]+\\.[A-Za-z0-9]+", 
              "h04", # change these to the desired heating/cooling group
              "\\.[0-9]+\\.jld2$", sep = "")
fnames <- function( td, jld) {
# Creates string that can be pasted directly into julia for MD2.heatcool()
  # td is the target directory, jld is the regex to match
  # jld <- paste( "^[A-Za-z0-9]+\\.[A-Za-z0-9]+", 
  #           "h04", # change these to the desired heating/cooling group
  #           "\\.[0-9]+\\.jld2$", sep = "")

   f <- dir( td, jld)
   ll <- t( vapply( f, function(x) unlist(strsplit( x, "\\.")), 
                   c("series","energy","exec","ext")))
   #rownames( ll) <- NULL
   colnames( ll) <- c("Series","Energy","Exec","Ext")
   f2 <- data.table( ll, keep.rownames=TRUE)
   #er <- unique( f2$energy)
   f2$EN <- as.numeric( f2$Exec) # convert Exec to numbers
   f3 <- f2[ f2[ , .I[EN == max(EN)], by = Energy]$V1]$rn
   # above line find the max EN by Energy, and returns rowname.
   cat( '["', 
        paste( substring( f3, 1, nchar( f3) - 5), collapse = '", "'), 
        '"]', sep="")
}
fnames( td, jld)
```

The explanation of the regex is as follows. `^[A-Za-z0-9]+` identifies
the *series* group that must start the string. While it can contain
anything, the three groups must all exist, ending with ".jld2". Each
"\\." requires a "dot" to be present, and the `[A-Za-z0-9]+` identifies
the *energy* group (which also can contain anything) followed by
`[0-9]+` which identifies the *exec* group, which can only contain
number characters. Thus "abcd.a1b2.1234.jld2" is a proper name, while
"abcd.a1b2.jld2" is not (the "exec" group is missing.) In the above, the
characters "h04" are added to the energy group to filter only those
files with those characters in the energy group.

``` julia
 "S3.0046h05.0106"
```

We ran 120,000 steps for all runs this time.

```{r}
#| label: DFfile7
MD2DF.M7 <- MD2DFfile( "../MD2DF.M7.RDS", td, "S3*.????h??.????.scalars.csv",
                       df = MD2DF.M, verbose = TRUE)

mgp = c(1.7, 0.4, 0))

par(op)
MD2DF.M7[grepl( "h06", run) & valid==0, run]
```

Interestingly, `S3.0045h06` appears to be valid. We will extend the
remaining three to 4M steps. We need to run
`r  (4000000 - 120000)/50000` 50k step executions, so we'll run 78.\`

``` julia
julia> @time MD2.filerun_thread( td, ["S3.0043h06", "S3.0044h06", "S3.0046h06"],
12, 50000, 78)
734.529886 seconds (701.53 M allocations: 44.296 GiB, 2.18% gc time, 
22 lock conflicts)

julia> 
```

Since we ran to 4M steps, we really don't need to check these, but we
will look at the first, just to check what may have happened.

```{r}
#| label: er004306
#| fig.cap: "Extended run for `S3.0043h06` to 4M steps."
x <- combineruns( td,"S3","0043h06",verbose=TRUE)
plotMD2( x$rundt)
xproc <- procMD2DF(x, 1000)
xproc[ , .(total.steps, steps.avg, TE.mean.rs, ke.mean.rs, valid)]
rm(x)
```

`S3.0043h06` appears to be solidifying (($\psi_6$ is bouncing around
0.6). Let's take an inventory of the `h06` runs.

```{r}
#| label: DFfile8
MD2DF.M8 <- MD2DFfile( "../MD2DF.M8.RDS", td, "S3*.????h??.????.scalars.csv",
                       df = MD2DF.M, verbose = TRUE)

mgp = c(1.7, 0.4, 0))

par(op)
knitr::kable( MD2DF.M8[grepl( "h06", run), 
                       .(run, TE=TE.mean.rs, Temp=ke.mean.rs, valid,
                         total.steps, steps.avg)])
```

The colder runs are clearly not in the solid/fluid transition region
yet, so we don't need to run these to 120K steps yet. Since essentially
all runs are in the solid region, the cadence will be to run to 60K
steps, check validity, and then double the steps of runs not vald.

```{r}
              "\\.[0-9]+\\.jld2$", sep = "")

```

# Quick Analysis

We now have nine initialization series to examine: the first with an
initialization for each point, four which have been heated, and four
which have been cooled.

`S!` and `S2` series are all individual initializations. The `S3` and
`S3b` series whose energies do not have an "h" in the field are also
individual initializations. Those with the "h" are heated or cooled for
the initialization energy in the name. Thus `S3.0008h12` is the twelfth
heating of `S3.0008`. We did not distinguish in the names which were
heating and which were cooling. The code below will add a tag `itype`
(initialization type) to call the series as `Init`, `Heat`, or `Cool`.

```{r}
#| label: MD2DFN
MD2DF.N <- data.table::copy(MD2DF.Ml)
MD2DF.N$itype <- with( MD2DF.N, 
      ifelse( series %in% c("S1","S2"), "Init",
            ifelse( !grepl( "h", energy), "Init",
                    ifelse( grepl( "0008|0009|0010|0011", energy), 
                            "Heat", "Cool")
                    )
            )
      )
saveRDS( MD2DF.N, "../MD2DF.N.RDS" )
```

The heated and cooled files track the raw initialization files very
well(#fig-MD2DFKplot).

```{r}
#| label: fig-MD2DFKplot
#| fig.cap: "Plot of the kinetic energy vs. pressure for all `S3` runs between $T = 0.004$ and $T = 0.02$. Red points are those not considered valid."
pchlu <- c( Init = 1, Heat = 0, Cool = 2) # pch lookup
with( MD2DF.N[ grepl( "S3", series, fixed = TRUE) & 
                  ke.mean.rs %within% c( 0.004, 0.02),], {
   col = ifelse( valid, "black", "red")
   plot( y = Pressure.mean.rs, x = ke.mean.rs, col = col,
      xlab = "T", ylab = "Pressure", pch =  pchlu[ itype],
      main = "Pressure vs Temperature for S3 runs",
      panel.first = grid())
   })
legend( "bottomright", legend = names( pchlu), pch = pchlu)
```

#fig-MD2DFKplotz zooms into the transition region.

```{r}
#| label: fig-MD2DFKplotz
#| fig.cap: "Zoom into #fig-MD2DFKplot. Red points are those not considered valid."
with( MD2DF.N[ grepl( "S3", series, fixed = TRUE) & 
                  ke.mean.rs %within% c( 0.007, 0.015),], {
   col = ifelse( valid, "black", "red")
   plot( y = Pressure.mean.rs, x = ke.mean.rs, col = col,
      xlab = "T", ylab = "Pressure", pch =  pchlu[ itype],
      main = "Pressure vs Temperature for S3 runs",
      panel.first = grid())
   })
legend( "bottomright", legend = names( pchlu), pch = pchlu)
```

#fig-Kpsivt shows the Nelson Halperin order parameter vs. temperature
around the transition region.

```{r}
#| label: fig-Kpsivt
#| fig.cap: "Nelson Halperin order parameter vs. temperature. Red points are those not considered valid."
with( MD2DF.N[ grepl( "S3", series, fixed = TRUE) & 
                  ke.mean.rs %within% c( 0.007, 0.015),], {
   col = ifelse( valid, "black", "red")
   plot( y = psiabs.mean.rs, x = ke.mean.rs, col = col,
      xlab = "T", ylab = expression( psi), pch =  pchlu[ itype],
      main = "NHOP vs Temperature for S3 runs",
      panel.first = grid())
   })
legend( "bottomleft", legend = names( pchlu), pch = pchlu)
```

#fig-Kesdvt shows the variance of the temperature vs. temperature around
the transition region.

```{r}
#| label: fig-Kesdvt
#| fig.cap: "Variance of T vs. temperature. Red points are those not considered valid."
with( MD2DF.N[ grepl( "S3", series, fixed = TRUE) & 
                  ke.mean.rs %within% c( 0.007, 0.015),], {
   col = ifelse( valid, "black", "red")
   plot( y = ke.sd.rs, x = ke.mean.rs, col = col,
      xlab = "T", ylab = expression( sigma), pch =  pchlu[ itype],
      main = "Variance of T vs Temperature for S3 runs",
      panel.first = grid())
   })
legend( "topleft", legend = names( pchlu), pch = pchlu)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tvTE
#| fig.cap: "Temperature vs total energy . Red points are those not considered valid."
with( MD2DF.N[ grepl( "S3", series, fixed = TRUE) & 
                  ke.mean.rs %within% c( 0.007, 0.015),], {
   col = ifelse( valid, "black", "red")
   plot( y = ke.mean.rs, x = TE.mean.rs, col = col,
      xlab = "Total Energy", ylab = "T", pch =  pchlu[ itype],
      main = "Temperature Total Energy for S3 runs",
      panel.first = grid())
   })
legend( "topleft", legend = names( pchlu), pch = pchlu)
```
